🇪🇹⚔️ Rebels push deeper into Ethiopia as government seeks urgent reinforcements
The Ethiopian government plans to withdraw more than 3,000 troops from Somalia and redeploy them to counter a growing rebellion at home, Bloomberg reports.
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed is facing a coalition of seven armed and political groups, including the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), the Amhara Fano militia and the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA), which have formed the Alliance for Survival to oust the federal government. The rebels launched a major [offensive on September 23](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75072).
On September 28, Ethiopian federal forces seized Alamata, a town in the Tigray Region, and moved closer to the Tigrayan capital of Mekelle, held by rebels. While social media accounts have circulated videos purportedly showing weapons abandoned by the TPLF and its allies, the conflict appears to be only ramping up.
The same day, reports emerged that TPLF forces had seized Erebti and were advancing toward Afdera, as fighting spread beyond Tigray and Amhara into Afar. The rebels seek to oust the incumbent government, establish an inclusive transitional administration and pursue constitutional reform.
The Ethiopian government accuses Eritrea and Sudan of backing the rebels, charges both countries firmly deny. Sudan, in turn, accuses Ethiopia of supporting [the RSF](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/64367), which has been fighting the Sudanese government [since April 2023](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/55349).
Relations between Ethiopia and Eritrea have also soured, with PM Abiy Ahmed repeatedly hinting at plans to gain access to Red Sea coastline under Eritrean control by force.

events.text:
🇨🇳⚠📦 Pentagon In Panic: China Tests Hybrid Cargo Drone That Can Resupply Troops Without Landing
China has tested its YH-1000S heavy cargo drone in an airborne supply mission, dropping three medium containers and eight smaller loads during a single flight.
The aircraft remained stable throughout the operation and delivered the cargo with the required accuracy, demonstrating its ability to supply units without landing near them.
🔸 Eleven loads in one test: The drone released three medium-sized containers followed by eight smaller cargo packages. Maintaining stability during repeated drops is essential because every change in weight can affect an unmanned aircraft’s balance and flight path.
🔸 Hybrid power borrowed from China’s car industry: The YH-1000S uses a modified 2.0T hybrid powertrain developed with Chinese new-energy vehicle companies. Its batteries can reportedly keep the aircraft flying independently for around 30 minutes.
🔸 Shorter takeoff and landing distances: The hybrid system provides additional power during the most demanding stages of flight while increasing payload capacity and range. The drone still requires a suitable place to take off, although it needs less runway than a conventional cargo aircraft.
🔸 Supplies delivered without landing: A rear cargo door allows loads to be released in flight. Its position reduces disruption to the aircraft’s aerodynamics and helps the flight-control system remain stable as cargo leaves the drone.
🔸 Designed for rapid mission changes: The rear section can accommodate modular cargo compartments for different loads. The same aircraft could carry food, medical supplies, communications equipment or other urgently needed cargo.
🔸 Built for cheaper production: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation says automotive components, shared supply chains and modular manufacturing have reduced development and production costs. That could make the YH-1000S easier to manufacture in larger numbers.
CASC presents the aircraft primarily as a platform for commercial logistics, disaster relief, weather modification and maritime monitoring. Its ability to deliver supplies from the air also gives it clear military value.
Roads, ports and local airfields are among the first targets in a conflict. Cargo drones could take off from safer locations and release supplies directly near dispersed units without risking pilots or attempting a landing under fire.

🇮🇷🚀 ‘Hit-and-run’ era over as Iran boosts missile capacity – IRGC adviser
Iran can now fire as many missiles as needed to achieve its objectives, IRGC Aerospace Force adviser Brigadier General Ali Balali said.
Balali pointed to the severe limitations on Iran’s missile capabilities during the 1980-1988 war with Iraq.
“During the eight years of the Sacred Defense, we fired a total of 88 missiles,” he said.
Iranian forces had to ration their missiles to sustain operations until the end of the war, the brigadier general explained.
“Today, in every operation, the [Iranian] armed forces launch as many [missiles] as necessary, with power and determination, so that the enemy is disciplined and understands that the era of ‘hit and run’ is over,” Balali stressed.
Presently, Iran’s missile production allows it to sustain operations at the launch rate seen during the recent war, even if a confrontation lasts for several years, he added.

events.text:
✈️🇨🇳 New Chinese missile guidance system could beat F-35 jets
The lidar-based system developed by a team led by Li Zhiyuan of the China Airborne Missile Academy could ostensibly detect and track an F-35 combat aircraft at a distance of up to 61.5 kilometers, the South China Morning Post notes.
While the US stealth aircraft’s coating makes it very difficult to detect with more conventional radars, it does not offer the same protection against a single-photon lidar that essentially uses reflected laser light to detect the target.
This development does have a few caveats, however:
🌏 The Chinese team’s findings come from a computer simulation, so such targeting device is yet to be truly tested
🌏 The focused beam utilized by the lidar to locate the target is unlikely to function as an early-warning system
🌏 The 61.5km maximum range of the detection system still puts it within the reach of the long-range missiles used by a F-35

⚔️📑 Houthis push to seize key strategic mountains overlooking Bab el-Mandeb
Ansar Allah has launched fresh assaults on pro-Saudi forces across the mountains of Lahj’s Al-Madaribah wa Ra’as Al-Arah district, seeking to capture three interconnected heights overlooking the strait’s inland approaches.
On September 29, clashes intensified around Al-Aghbara Mountain as the Houthis sought to sever key supply routes linking Saudi-backed positions in Lahj and Taiz, Arab News reports.
Hostilities around Kahboub Mountain are also continuing. Control of the area could allow Ansar Allah to consolidate its gains along the Red Sea coast and threaten roads leading toward Aden, where the Saudi-backed Yemeni administration is based.
Kahboub has emerged as a key Houthi target since the group solidified control over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on September 10. The mountain commands the strait, the coastal city of Dhubab and Perim Island.
Jabal Naman is another strategically vital mountain on the Lahj-Taiz border that the Houthis are seeking to seize and hold.
Ansar Allah is also reinforcing its military in apparent preparation for another major offensive on Taiz, a pro-Saudi officer told the publication, describing the Houthi buildup – including tanks, other military equipment and missiles – as “massive.”
